text:
Maya: Noticed p95 < p50 on /v1/embeddings in us-east after the warm-pool routing change. p95=130ms, p50=210ms. Weird.
Jordan: Can you paste the query/window?
Maya: Ran: ```SELECT sample_origin, count(*) raw_count, approx_percentile(response_ms,0.95) p95, approx_percentile(response_ms,0.5) p50 FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/embeddings' AND ts > now()-30m GROUP BY sample_origin;``` Warm-pool shows p95=20 p50=15, primary shows p95=420 p50=200. Merge gives inverted ordering.
Ravi: Classic sampler bias + naive tdigest merge. Raw counts favor warm-pool because of sampling multiplier.
Claire: Also bucket interpolation can make it worse.
Maya: Short-term: console should show per-origin percentiles by default for endpoints with high origin variance and add a yellow flag when p95 < p50.
Jordan: Medium-term: telemetry should carry origin_weights and perform a weight-aware merge or compute weighted histograms.
Ravi: I'll open telemetry PR to add origin_weights and weight-aware tdigest merge.
Claire: I'll add a console toggle "percentile provenance" (merged / per-origin / weighted) behind a flag.
MetricsBot: Created INC-2026-031: "percentile-ordering-oddity-us-east-embeddings" tasks: telemetry schema, console toggle, runbook. Link: https://redwood/internal/inc/INC-2026-031
Maya: Adding eng-runtime to pre-rollout checklist: run a telemetry smoke check to ensure merged percentiles don't invert across a 10m test window.
Ravi: For runbook, include quick SQL to compare per-origin vs merged and instructions to compute a weighted merge.
Claire: We'll ship console toggle behind FF next deploy. :rocket:
